headline: GRAINS SIT STILL, CATTLE SLIP AGAIN BEFORE COF
lead: Corn eased to $5.17, beans barely moved at $13.04, and neither market gave you a reason to do anything today. Cattle is the real story: down 0.8% to $218.95, a second straight session lower with USDA's Cattle on Feed still hours away at 2:00 PM CT.
teaser: Grains go quiet, cattle keeps sliding into a Cattle on Feed report that hasn't printed yet.

one_number.context: Reuters' regular count found just 9 carriers transited Thursday, eight of them outbound, the thinnest tally yet as the Iran-Hormuz cycle grinds on.

yesterdays_call.note: Crude drifted to $92.96, not the $94.50 line; the Hormuz premium is still failing to build despite the thin traffic count.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called crude up toward $94.50 ($93.19 when the call was made). It closed at $92.96.

action: Live cattle at $218.95: nothing to do ahead of Cattle on Feed at 2:00 PM CT, but a close under $216.50 is the next sell.

sections.title: Cattle Slips Again, Report Looms
sections.body:
- Live cattle gave back another 0.8% to **$218.95**, second straight lower close heading into today's Cattle on Feed at 2:00 PM CT.
- Farm Bureau renewed its push against the extra 300,000 metric tons of beef import allowance Wednesday, a policy fight that hasn't moved cash cattle yet.
sections.so_what: Two red closes ahead of data means the market is de-risking, not predicting the report.

sections.title: Grains Stay Parked
sections.body:
- Corn eased 0.4% to **$5.17**, beans barely ticked down to $13.04, both markets described by feedstuffs.com as quiet amid ongoing US-China trade talks.
- No fresh confirmed China purchase news today to push beans, and no weather story to push corn; the calendar is empty and the tape knows it.
sections.so_what: Quiet grains with US-China talks unresolved means the next move is news-driven, not chart-driven.

outside_the_pit.title: VLCC rates hit record $1.27 million a day
outside_the_pit.body: Ship-to-ship transfer capacity off Oman is maxed out after Saudi Arabia rerouted flows from Yanbu around Houthi attacks, pushing freight costs that eventually hit diesel.

watch_list.desc: Cattle on Feed; on-feed number above year-ago keeps the placement story alive, below tightens the setup further.
Crop Progress; corn harvest pace above 20% keeps the Belt on schedule for a normal wrap-up.
Hormuz transit count; another single-digit day like Thursday's 9 vessels adds freight premium to diesel.

daily_quote.text: Throw no stones into the well that gives you water.

source_summary: CME/CBOT settlement data, USDA, feedstuffs.com, oilprice.com, thefencepost.com, beefmagazine.com, world-grain.com, Reuters
